comparisons.peer_summary: Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $19.1 billion increased nine percent, primarily driven by higher asset management fees due to higher average equity market valuations and positive AUM flows, as well as higher brokerage fees due to increased transactional volume.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Bank of America (BAC) report significant revenue growth in their respective wealth management segments driven by market performance and assets under management (AUM). GS’s Asset & Wealth Management net revenues increased 16% to $16.14 billion, primarily driven by higher Management and other fees. Similarly, BAC’s Merrill Wealth Management revenue increased 9% to $19.1 billion, primarily driven by higher asset management fees due to higher average equity market valuations and positive AUM flows. While GS also cites higher Private banking and lending revenues, BAC highlights brokerage fees from transactional volume, but both identify fee growth linked to market conditions and AUM as a core driver.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Non-Interest Expense Trend and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth Management non-interest expenses increased 5% to $20,618 million in 2024 compared to the prior year. This increase was driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses, primarily due to increased formulaic payouts to representatives on higher compensable revenues, partially offset by decreases in non-compensation expenses such as professional services, legal expenses, and FDIC special assessment costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose trends in operating expenses within their wealth management divisions, linking compensation costs to revenue performance. GS reports that while overall operating expenses in Asset & Wealth Management decreased 9%, this was partially offset by higher compensation and benefits expenses reflecting improved operating performance. MS reports that Wealth Management non-interest expenses increased 5%, driven primarily by higher compensation and benefits due to increased formulaic payouts to representatives on higher compensable revenues. Both firms demonstrate that as revenues improve or increase, compensation expenses rise in correlation.

sentences.text: Operating expenses were $11.83 billion for 2024, 9% lower than 2023, due to significantly lower expenses, including impairments, related to commercial real estate in CIEs, partially offset by higher compensation and benefits expenses (reflecting improved operating performance).

Non-interest expenses of $20,618 million in 2024 increased 5% compared with the prior year, as a result of higher Compensation and benefits expenses, partially offset by lower Non-compensation expenses.
